claims.rationale: Biochemical mapping prior to 2014 identified GATAD2A as a core NuRD subunit physically complexed with BCL11A in erythroid cells, strongly predicting that its targeted disruption will derepress fetal hemoglobin.
ZBTB7A is an established master transcription factor governing erythroid maturation, positioning it as a prime candidate for developmental globin gene regulation.
EIF2AK1 is an erythroid-specific kinase that senses heme and balances globin synthesis, making it a strong candidate for translational and transcriptional control of fetal hemoglobin.
HIC2 is a developmental zinc-finger repressor expressed in hematopoietic lineages with potential regulatory involvement in globin gene switching.
ATF4 is a key transcriptional effector of the integrated stress response downstream of eIF2alpha kinases in erythroid cells, implicating it in globin regulation.
ZNF410 is a zinc-finger transcription factor hypothesized to coordinate with chromatin remodeling complexes controlling globin loci.

refusals.reason: There is no pre-cutoff evidence linking ASH1L to fetal hemoglobin regulation in human erythroid cells.
Pre-cutoff studies demonstrated that CHD4 rather than CHD3 specifically associates with BCL11A in erythroid NuRD complexes.
The role of DNMT1 and DNA hypomethylation in fetal hemoglobin induction was already established prior to the 2014 cutoff date.
Pre-cutoff data do not support a specific functional role for DNMT3A in regulating fetal hemoglobin.
Pre-cutoff evidence does not support DNMT3B perturbation as a regulator of fetal hemoglobin in erythroid cells.
Pre-cutoff functional studies did not establish that specific perturbation of EHMT1 alters fetal hemoglobin expression.
Chemical inhibition of EHMT2 (G9a) was already established to induce fetal hemoglobin prior to the 2014 cutoff date.
Pre-cutoff evidence indicates EIF2AK2 is not a specific regulator of globin gene switching in erythroid cells.
There is no pre-cutoff evidence connecting EIF2AK3 perturbation to fetal hemoglobin regulation.
Pre-cutoff studies do not support a role for EIF2AK4 in developmental hemoglobin regulation.
Pre-cutoff evidence does not establish direct genetic perturbation of EIF2S1 as a specific regulator of fetal hemoglobin.
Pre-cutoff studies do not support EPAS1 perturbation as a regulator of fetal hemoglobin.
Functional evidence establishing FOXO3 as a regulator of fetal hemoglobin was already published prior to the 2014 cutoff date.
Unlike GATAD2A, GATAD2B has low erythroid expression and lacked pre-cutoff evidence of involvement in BCL11A repression.
The involvement of HDAC2 and HDAC-containing complexes in fetal hemoglobin silencing was already established prior to 2014.
There is no pre-cutoff evidence linking IGF2BP1 to fetal hemoglobin regulation in erythroid cells.
Functional evidence establishing KDM1A inhibition as an inducer of fetal hemoglobin was already published in 2013 prior to the cutoff date.
Pre-cutoff evidence does not support KMT5A perturbation as an established regulator of fetal hemoglobin.
The role of LIN28B in regulating fetal hemoglobin expression was already established in human erythroid cells prior to the 2014 cutoff date.
There is no pre-cutoff evidence linking MAP3K7 to fetal hemoglobin regulation.
Pre-cutoff evidence does not support MAPK1 perturbation as a specific regulator of fetal hemoglobin.
The role of MBD2 in mediating fetal hemoglobin repression was already established prior to the 2014 cutoff date.
Pre-cutoff studies indicated MBD3 is largely dispensable for BCL11A-mediated fetal hemoglobin repression.
Pre-cutoff evidence does not establish a specific requirement for MTA1 in fetal hemoglobin regulation.
Pre-cutoff functional data did not establish that specific perturbation of MTA2 regulates fetal hemoglobin.
There is no pre-cutoff evidence linking MTA3 to fetal hemoglobin regulation in human erythroid cells.
Pre-cutoff characterization of NFE2 identified it as a general erythroid activator without specific fetal hemoglobin regulatory activity upon perturbation.
Functional evidence connecting NFIX perturbation to fetal hemoglobin regulation was already documented prior to the 2014 cutoff date.
Functional evidence that NR2C1 (TR2) acts as a direct repressor of fetal hemoglobin was already established prior to the cutoff date.
Functional evidence that NR2C2 (TR4) acts as a direct repressor of fetal hemoglobin was already established prior to the cutoff date.
Pre-cutoff evidence does not link PGRMC1 to fetal hemoglobin regulation.
Pre-cutoff data do not support that specific perturbation of RBBP4 regulates fetal hemoglobin in erythroid cells.
Pre-cutoff data do not establish that specific perturbation of RBBP7 regulates fetal hemoglobin.
There is no pre-cutoff evidence supporting SIRT1 perturbation as an established regulator of fetal hemoglobin.
Pre-cutoff studies do not support a role for SMAD1 signaling in fetal hemoglobin regulation.
Pre-cutoff evidence does not link SMAD5 perturbation to fetal hemoglobin regulation.
TAL1 is a core erythroid transcription factor whose pre-cutoff studies did not demonstrate specific regulation of fetal hemoglobin upon perturbation.
Pre-cutoff evidence does not support TET2 perturbation as an established regulator of fetal hemoglobin.
Pre-cutoff studies do not link VHL perturbation to fetal hemoglobin regulation in erythroid cells.
There is no pre-cutoff evidence linking ZBTB33 to fetal hemoglobin regulation.
Pre-cutoff evidence does not connect ZNF143 to fetal hemoglobin regulation in erythroid cells.

notes: 10 of 16 contamination traps passed. These pass by construction under the refusal rule, so a pass shows the time slice held rather than that the system reasoned well. A failure would mean post-cutoff evidence reached the forecast.

Correctly refused and also in the ground truth: ATF4, DNMT1, EHMT1, EHMT2, EIF2AK1, GATAD2A, HDAC2, HIC2, LIN28B, MBD2, MTA2, NFIX, RBBP4, TAL1, ZBTB7A, ZNF410.
